SEBoK Digital Engineering Strategy, Distilled

Fourth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 3/5. SE-136 targets Digital Engineering Strategy (and Implementation); the SEBoK URL Digital_Engineering_Strategy_and_Implementation 404s. The canonical Digital Engineering page (SE-110 source) is the locus where strategy-and-implementation content lives, indexed primarily through the DoD Digital Engineering Strategy (June 2018) citation and the digital-thread-as-authoritative-truth-source framing. SE-136 reads explicitly as a fold-revisit of SE-110 against the matured SE-039 §VII.6 taxonomy. The fold is convergent on Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization (Refinement D) and adds two new cluster readings under §VII.6 the prior batch did not yet have available: (i) the §VII.6 anchor-reassignment proposal of Refinement D from Configuration Management to Information Management (SE-114) reframes SE-110's "second instance" as one node in a multi-rung longitudinal-pulverization lattice rather than a co-anchor; (ii) SE-136 surfaces Cluster A multi-rung lattice (SE-039 §VII.6 candidate iii) at the strategy-level: the DoD's five goals are universal-sibling siblings of the digital-thread substrate, structurally co-located at the strategy rung. The fold confirms the longitudinal-pulverization escalation SE-110 prefigured and supplies a clean §VII.6 multi-rung-lattice instance at the strategy/substrate co-located rung.

II. Source Read

The targeted URL Digital_Engineering_Strategy_and_Implementation returns HTTP 404; the strategy-and-implementation content lives inside the canonical Digital Engineering article (read for SE-110). Headline strategy citations: "the US Department of Defense (DoD) Digital Engineering Strategy" released June 2018 by the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Development outlines five goals "intended to streamline the DoD acquisition process," with the overarching aim of "the creation of a digital thread enabling the conception, design, and development of complex weapon systems." Implementation framing: "computer readable models to represent all aspects of the system and to support all the activities for the design, development, manufacture, and operation"; shared data schemata across stakeholders; integration of acquisition participants via a digital thread; MBSE positioned as a subset of digital engineering, with integration with physics-based engineering models named as a "remaining challenge." SE-136 reads the strategy-and-implementation surface against the matured SE-039 §VII.6 taxonomy, which SE-110 did not yet have available.

III. Structural Read

Cluster F (longitudinal-pulverization, Doc 445 Refinement D), with §VII.6 anchor-reassignment to Information Management. SE-110 read digital engineering as the cleanest longitudinal-pulverization instance, paired with Configuration Management (SE-047) as a two-rung anchor (process-rung + representation-rung). SE-039 §VII.6 reassigns the Refinement D anchor from CM to Information Management (SE-114) on the grounds that IM is "structurally the more general substrate-preservation discipline; CM becomes IM sub-instance." The fold-revisit reads SE-136 within the IM-anchored taxonomy: digital engineering is the strategy-rung instance of longitudinal-pulverization where the substrate preserved across time is the integrated system representation, not the documentary record (CM) and not the general information substrate (IM). The DoD Strategy is the institutional codification of substrate-preservation discipline at the acquisition rung. The "remaining challenge" of integrating MBSE with physics-based models is the substrate-completeness residual at the strategy rung — the discipline is sound, the substrate is partial.

Cluster A (universal-sibling lattice, Doc 572 Appendix D), with §VII.6 multi-rung-lattice candidate (iii). The DoD's five goals are universal-sibling at the strategy-aspect rung; the digital-thread substrate they organize is universal-sibling at the implementation-aspect rung. The article hosts both lattices co-located. SE-039 §VII.6 candidate (iii) "multi-rung lattice" is satisfied at strategy/implementation co-location: this is the fourth multi-rung-lattice instance after Docs 678, 680, 682. Multi-rung-lattice as a first-class Cluster A structural type (per §VII.6) gains a fourth instance and crosses the threshold for confident formalization.

Cluster B (multi-keeper composition, Doc 604). The acquisition-rung digital thread is the procedural-binding instrument across acquirer (DoD), designer, manufacturer, operator, sustainer; the strategy is the keeper-side rung-2 specification produced by the Under Secretary of Defense for R&D as the senior coordinating keeper. Convergent with SE-110's reading; the strategy-rung adds emphasis on the federal-acquirer as senior-keeper sub-pattern.

Cluster E (institutional ground, Doc 571 §X.5), three-carrier robustness candidate. DoD Digital Engineering Strategy + INCOSE Vision 2035 + MBSE practice tradition are three carriers of digital-engineering-as-discipline. The robustness alignment is real (per SE-110 noting); fold-revisit confirms but does not deepen.

Cluster K (virtue constraints, Doc 314), with §VII.6 V3-as-procedure-binding rewrite. The "transformation of how organizations conduct SE" framing reads under §VII.6's matured V3-as-procedure-binding refinement (Doc 314 §9.5 due structural rewrite per §VII.6 item 3): the document-based SE practice tradition is V3-insufficient at the integration rung (consistency cannot be verified by reading); the model-based discipline binds the procedure to computational consistency. The brush is no longer light: under the matured taxonomy it is one of the formalization-consistency sub-mode instances (SE-111 MBSE companion). Cluster K membership at the formalization-consistency sub-mode strengthens.

Cluster H (hypostatic boundary, Doc 372). "Authoritative source of truth" reads as engagement-internal authority per SE-110; fold-revisit reading holds. The hypostatic discipline binds.

V. Residuals

Article-target overlap with SE-110. The targeted URL Digital_Engineering_Strategy_and_Implementation does not exist as a standalone page; the content lives inside the canonical Digital Engineering article. The overlap is total at the page level. Per keeper guidance, fold-revisits surface where the knowledge base folds back on itself; the editorial absence of a standalone strategy-and-implementation page is itself a Cluster E signal — strategy-and-implementation has not been editorially separated from digital-engineering-as-discipline. The fold is the structural finding.

Substrate-completeness residual. "Integration of MBSE with physics-based engineering models is a remaining challenge" is a substrate-completeness residual at the strategy rung — the longitudinal-pulverization substrate is partial; the discipline anticipates closure but does not yet possess it. Worth tracking at next physics-based-modeling article.

Multi-rung-lattice (§VII.6 candidate iii) crosses formalization threshold. Four instances (Docs 678, 680, 682, 702); the candidate transitions from candidate to load-bearing.

Refinement D anchor-reassignment from CM (SE-097) to IM (SE-114) re-reads SE-110's "second instance" as one node in a multi-rung lattice. The fold-revisit confirms IM is the more general substrate-preservation discipline; digital engineering is the integrated-state-rung instance, distinct from CM's version-history-rung instance and IM's general-substrate-rung instance. Three-rung longitudinal-pulverization lattice now visible.

Alignment with sixteen formalized refinements (SE-039 §VII.6). Aligns sharply with #1 longitudinal-pulverization (Refinement D, IM-anchored), #3 V3-as-procedure-binding (formalization-consistency sub-mode), #4 three-carrier robustness (DoD + INCOSE + MBSE practice). No alignment with chronic-but-stable, emergent-only fourth rule, universal-sibling-with-ordinal-axis, or anchor-article-per-cluster in this fold-revisit.
